'''Denis Noble''' (born 16 November 1936) is a British [[Physiology|physiologist]] and [[biologist]] who held the [[John Burdon-Sanderson|Burdon Sanderson]] Chair of [[Circulatory system|Cardiovascular Physiology]] at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1984 to 2004 and was appointed professor emeritus and co-director of computational physiology.<ref name="homepage">[http://noble.physiol.ox.ac.uk/People/DNoble/ Biography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060425143248/http://noble.physiol.ox.ac.uk/People/Dnoble/ |date=25 April 2006 }}, Denis Noble homepage.</ref><ref name=":1">{{YouTube|id=glUjhYDZUgM|title= Music of Life lecture in Maribor 2012}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|id=MzD1daWq4ng|title= Lecture on Evolution IUPS Opening plenary 2013}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1113/expphysiol.2012.071134| title = Physiology is rocking the foundations of evolutionary biology| journal = Experimental Physiology| pages = 1235–1243| year = 2013| last1 = Noble | first1 = D.| pmid=23585325| volume=98| issue = 8| s2cid = 19689192| doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1152/ajpheart.00794.2003| pmid = 14656705| title = A model for human ventricular tissue| journal = AJP: Heart and Circulatory Physiology| volume = 286| issue = 4| pages = H1573–H1589| year = 2003| last1 = Ten Tusscher | first1 = K. H. W. J.}}</ref> Since 2025, he is a Distinguished Chair Professor at [[Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology|Daegu-Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology]] (DGIST).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-03-01 |title=Professor Denis Noble, a Distinguished Scholar in Physiology from Oxford University, Ignites Bio Research in Daegu-Gyeongbuk |url=https://www.asiaresearchnews.com/content/professor-denis-noble-distinguished-scholar-physiology-oxford-university-ignites-bio |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=Asia Research News |language=en}}</ref>

In 2014, Noble established The Third Way of Evolution (TWE) project with [[James A. Shapiro]] which rejects [[natural selection]] as the primary cause of [[evolution]] and predicts that the entire framework of the [[Modern synthesis (20th century)|modern synthesis of evolution]] will be replaced,<ref name="Svensson 2023" /> though these claims have not gained support from mainstream evolutionary biology, and TWE has been described as a "[[fringe movement]]".<ref name="Svensson 2023" />

==Education==
Noble was educated at [[Emanuel School]] and [[University College London]] (UCL).<ref name="whoswho"/><ref name="homepage"/> In 1958 he began his investigations into the mechanisms of heartbeat. This led to two seminal papers in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' in 1960<ref name="sem1"/><ref name="sem2"/> giving the first experimentally-based mathematical simulation of the electrical rhythm of the heart.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Denis | year = 1962 | title = A modification of the Hodgkin—Huxley equations applicable to Purkinje fibre action and pacemaker potentials | journal = The Journal of Physiology | volume = 160 | issue = 2 | pages = 317–352 | doi=10.1113/jphysiol.1962.sp006849| pmid = 14480151 | pmc = 1359535 }}</ref>  In 1961 he obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] working under the supervision of [[Otto Hutter]] at UCL.<ref name="phd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Denis|last=Noble |title=Ion conductance of cardiac muscle |publisher=University College London |date=1962 |url=http://www.theses.com|authorlink=Denis Noble}}{{subscription required}}</ref><ref>Dennis Noble (2006). ''The Music of Life'', {{ISBN|0-19-929573-5}}</ref>

This work was subsequently developed extensively with [[Richard Tsien]] in 1975,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = McAllister | first1 = Eric | last2 = Noble | first2 = Denis | last3 = Tsien | first3 = Richard | year = 2022 | title = Reconstruction of the electrical activity of cardiac Purkinje fibres. | journal = Journal of Physiology| volume = 251 | issue = 1 | pages = 1–59 | doi=10.1113/jphysiol.1975.sp011080| pmid = 1185607 | pmc = 1348375 }}</ref> and with [[Dario DiFrancesco]] in 1985,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = DiFrancesco | first1 = Dario | last2 = Noble | first2 = Denis | year = 2022 | title = A model of cardiac electrical activity incorporating ionic pumps and concentration changes | journal = Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B | volume = 307 | issue = 1133 | pages = 353–398 | doi=10.1098/rstb.1985.0001| pmid = 2578676 }}</ref> forming the foundations of modern electrophysiology of the heart. The 1985 article was included in 2015 in the Royal Society's 350-year celebration of the publication of ''[[Philosophical Transactions]]''.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Partridge | first1 = Linda | year = 2015 | title = Celebrating 350 years of Philosophical Transactions: life sciences papers| journal = Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B | volume = 370 | issue = 1666 | article-number = 20140380 | doi=10.1098/rstb.2014.0380| pmid = 25750243 | pmc = 4360128 }}</ref>

== Career ==
He began his career as an assistant lecturer in physiology at [[University College London]], also serving as vice-warden at the [[University of London]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Carney |first=Stephen |date=2004-07-01 |title=Denis Noble discusses his career in computational biology |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S174183640402414X |journal=Drug Discovery Today: BIOSILICO |volume=2 |issue=4 |pages=135–137 |doi=10.1016/S1741-8364(04)02414-X |issn=1741-8364|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1963, he joined [[Balliol College, Oxford]] as a fellow and tutor, later becoming head of its graduate centre  and vice-master.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denis Noble |url=https://www.dpag.ox.ac.uk/team/denis-noble |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=www.dpag.ox.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

From 1984 to 2004, he was [[Burdon Sanderson]] Professor of Cardiovascular Physiology at the [[University of Oxford]] and a professorial fellow at [[Balliol College]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dutton |first=Bill |date=2017-04-25 |title=Big Questions and Big Issues for the US and Britain: A Discussion with Voices from Oxford's Denis Noble and Sung Hee Kim |url=https://billdutton.me/2017/04/25/big-questions-and-big-issues-for-the-us-and-britain-a-discussion-with-voices-from-oxfords-denis-noble-and-sung-hee-kim/ |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=William H. Dutton |language=en-US}}</ref> He subsequently became emeritus professor and continued as director of computational physiology. He also held appointments at [[Xi'an Jiaotong University]] and [[Osaka University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Noble Denis |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Noble_Denis |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

Alongside his academic work, he led major research programmes, co-founded [[Campaign for Science and Engineering|Save British Science]], and served as editor-in-chief of ''[[Progress in Biophysics and Molecular Biology]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=From 'Save British Science', to 'CaSE', to the future |url=https://www.sciencecampaign.org.uk/membership/guest-blog/from-save-british-science-to-case-to-the-future/ |access-date=2026-04-21 |website=CaSE |language=en-GB}}</ref> He later became president of the [[International Union of Physiological Sciences]] and held editorial roles at ''[[Interface Focus]]'' and the Oxford Longevity Project.<ref name=":0" />

==Research==
Noble's research focuses on using [[Computer simulation|computer models]] of [[Organ (anatomy)|biological organs]] and organ systems to interpret function from the molecular level to the whole organism. Together with international collaborators, his team has used supercomputers to create the first virtual organ, the virtual heart.<ref name=economist>[http://www.economist.com/science/displayStory.cfm?story_id=10018596&fsrc=nwlptwfree All systems go] article in [[The Economist]] 25-Oct-2007 discussing Noble's work</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|7102287830}}</ref>

As secretary-general of the International Union of Physiological Sciences 1993–2001, he played a major role, together with Peter Hunter, in launching the [[Physiome]] Project, an international project to use computer simulations to create the quantitative physiological models necessary to interpret the [[genome]], and he was elected president of the IUPS at its world congress in [[Kyoto]] in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/abi.html|title=Auckland Bioengineering Institute - The University of Auckland|website=www.Auckland.ac.nz|access-date=15 April 2019}}</ref>

Noble is also a philosopher of biology, with many publications in journals and books of philosophy.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Denis | year = 1967 | title = Charles Taylor on Teleological Explanation | journal = Analysis | volume = 27 | issue = 3 | pages = 96–103 | doi=10.2307/3326802 | jstor = 3326802 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Denis | year = 1993 | title = The logic of life: the public perception of science and its threat to the values of society | journal = Science and Public Policy | doi=10.1093/spp/20.3.187 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Raymond | last2 = Noble | first2 = Denis | year = 2022 | title = Can reasons and values influence action: how might intentional agency work physiologically?| journal = Journal for General Philosophy of Science | volume = 52 | issue = 2 | pages = 277–295 | doi=10.1007/s10838-020-09525-3| s2cid = 228947493 | doi-access = free }}</ref> In a review of ''The Music of Life'', a book discussing  [[systems biology]], a colleague has stated that "by challenging the foundations of current biological sciences, he questions the central dogma, its unidirectional view of information flow, and its imposition of a bottom-up methodology for research in the life sciences."<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1126/science.1141807| title = How Central is the Genome?| journal = Science| volume = 317| issue = 5839| pages = 753–754| year = 2007| last1 = Werner | first1 = E.| s2cid = 82065292}}</ref>

The introduction to the 2023  book ''Evolution "On Purpose": Teleonomy in Living Systems'', co-edited by Noble along with [[Addy Pross]], [[Peter Corning]], [[Stuart Kauffman]], [[James A. Shapiro]] and Richard I. Vane-Wright, concludes with the claim that "[[Teleonomy]] in living systems is not, after all, only "apparent". It is a fundamental fact of life."<ref>{{cite book |last1=Corning |first1=P A |last2=Kauffman |first2=S A |last3=Noble |first3=D |last4=Shapiro |first4=J A |last5=Vane-Wright |first5=R I |last6=Pross |first6=A |title=Evolution "On Purpose": Teleonomy in Living Systems |date=2023 |publisher=MIT Press |location=USA |page=6 |isbn=978-0-262-37602-0 |url=https://direct.mit.edu/books/oa-edited-volume/5634/Evolution-On-Purpose-Teleonomy-in-Living-Systems |access-date=October 1, 2026}}</ref>

===Reductionism===
His 2006 book ''The Music of Life'' examines some of the basic aspects of systems biology, and is critical of the ideas of [[genetic determinism]] and genetic [[scientific reductionism|reductionism]].  He points out that there are many examples of [[feedback loop]]s and "[[downward causation]]" in biology, and that it is not reasonable to privilege one level of understanding over all others.<ref>''The Music of Life'', pp. 12-14</ref>

He argues that "the paradigms for genetic causality in biological systems are seriously confused" and that "The metaphors that served us well during the [[Molecular biology|molecular biological]] phase of recent decades have limited or even misleading impacts in the multilevel world of systems biology. New paradigms are needed if we are to succeed in unravelling multifactorial genetic causation at higher levels of physiological function and so to explain the phenomena that genetics was originally about."<ref>{{Cite journal| last1 = Noble | first1 = D.| title = Genes and causation| journal = Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences| volume = 366| issue = 1878| pages = 3001–3015| date=Sep 2008 | issn = 1364-503X| pmid = 18559318 | doi = 10.1098/rsta.2008.0086|bibcode = 2008RSPTA.366.3001N | s2cid = 17592966}}</ref>

===The Third Way of Evolution===
Noble has rejected [[natural selection]] as the primary mechanism of evolution, contrary to the longstanding consensus of evolutionary biologists, and has called for an [[extended evolutionary synthesis]],  known as The Third Way of Evolution (TWE), as a replacement for the [[Modern synthesis (20th century)|modern synthesis]].<ref name="Svensson 2023">{{cite book |last1=Svensson |first1=Erik I. |title=Evolutionary Biology: Contemporary and Historical Reflections Upon Core Theory |date=2023 |isbn=978-3-031-22027-2 |series=Evolutionary Biology – New Perspectives on Its Development |volume=6 |pages=173–217 |chapter=The Structure of Evolutionary Theory: Beyond Neo-Darwinism, Neo-Lamarckism and Biased Historical Narratives About the Modern Synthesis |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-22028-9_11 |chapter-url=https://ecoevorxiv.org/repository/view/4002/}}</ref><ref>[http://www.physoc.org/press-release/2014/theory-evolution-has-evolved "The theory of evolution has evolved"]. The Physiological Society.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-05-10 |title=Replace the Modern Synthesis (Neo-Darwinism): An Interview With Denis Noble |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/suzan-mazur/replace-the-modern-sythes_b_5284211.html |access-date=2025-07-02 |website=HuffPost |language=en}}</ref>

He has argued that from research in epigenetics, [[Inheritance of acquired characteristics|acquired characteristics can be inherited]] and in contrast to the modern synthesis, genetic change is "far from random" and not always [[Gradualism|gradual]]. He has also claimed that the [[central dogma of molecular biology]] has been broken as an "embodiment of the Weismann Barrier",<ref name="Noble2018">{{cite journal|last1=Noble|first1=Denis|title=Central Dogma or Central Debate?|journal=Physiology|volume=33|issue=4|year=2018|pages=246–249|issn=1548-9213|doi=10.1152/physiol.00017.2018|pmid=29873598|doi-access=free}}</ref> and a new synthesis will integrate research from physiology with evolutionary biology.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Denis | year = 2013 | title = Physiology is rocking the foundations of evolutionary biology | journal = Experimental Physiology | volume = 98 | issue = 8| pages = 1235–1243 | doi=10.1113/expphysiol.2012.071134 | pmid=23585325| s2cid = 19689192 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>[http://www.voicesfromoxford.org/video/physiology-and-the-revolution-in-evolutionary-biology/184 "Physiology and the revolution in Evolutionary Biology"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151202031454/http://www.voicesfromoxford.org/video/physiology-and-the-revolution-in-evolutionary-biology/184 |date=2 December 2015 }}. Voices from Oxford.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | pmc= 4048083 | journal = The Journal of Physiology | pmid=24882808 | doi=10.1113/jphysiol.2014.273151 | volume=592 | issue = 11 | title=Evolution evolves: physiology returns to centre stage | year=2014 | pages=2237–44 | last1 = Noble | first1 = D | last2 = Jablonka | first2 = E | last3 = Joyner | first3 = MJ | last4 = Müller | first4 = GB | last5 = Omholt | first5 = SW}}</ref><ref name="The Illusions of the Modern Synthes">{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Denis | year = 2021 | title = The Illusions of the Modern Synthesis | journal = Experimental Physiology| volume = 107 | issue = 9 | pages = 1015–1028 | doi=10.1113/EP090133 | doi-access = free | pmid = 35871280 | pmc = 9543272 | s2cid = 251019199 }}</ref><ref name="Modern Physiology vindicates Darwin">{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = Denis | year = 2022 | title = Modern Physiology vindicates Darwin's Dream | journal = Experimental Physiology | volume = 107 | issue = 9 | pages = 1015–1028 | doi=10.1113/EP090133 | doi-access = free | pmid = 35871280 | pmc = 9543272 | s2cid = 251019199 }}</ref>

Noble and [[James A. Shapiro]] established The Third Way of Evolution (TWE) project in 2014. The TWE which is also known as the "Integrated Synthesis" shares many similarities with the extended evolutionary synthesis but is more radical in its claims.<ref name="Svensson 2023"/> The TWE consists of a group of researchers who provide a "Third Way" alternative to [[creationism]] and the modern synthesis. The TWE predicts that the modern synthesis will be replaced with an entirely new evolutionary framework. Similar to the extended evolutionary synthesis (EES), advocates of TWE cite examples of [[developmental bias]], [[genetic assimilation]], [[niche construction]], non-genetic inheritance, [[phenotypic plasticity]] and other evolutionary processes.<ref name="Svensson 2023"/> The concept of [[natural genetic engineering]], a process which Shapiro proposed to account for novelty created in biological evolution, is also important for the TWE.<ref name="The Illusions of the Modern Synthes"/><ref name="Modern Physiology vindicates Darwin"/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Shapiro J, Noble D|year=2021|title=What prevents mainstream evolutionists teaching the whole truth about how genomes evolve?|journal=Prog Biophys Mol Biol|volume=165|issue=|pages=140–152|doi=10.1016/j.pbiomolbio.2021.04.004|pmid=33933502}}</ref> The difference between the extended synthesis and the TWE is that the latter calls for an entire replacement of the modern synthesis rather than an extension.<ref name="Svensson 2023"/>

In 2023, evolutionary biologist Erik Svensson commented that "to date, there are few leading evolutionary biologists who have openly embraced the TWE" and it is unlikely that an entire replacement of the modern synthesis will occur as there has been little visibility of such a forthcoming [[paradigm shift]] during the past decade, and described TWE as a "[[fringe movement]] outside mainstream evolutionary biology" that is ideologically adjacent to [[Lamarckism]]. Svensson described Noble's claims as based on "biased and historically misleading characterizations" of the modern evolutionary synthesis, conflating it with both the earlier "[[Neo-Darwinism]]", as well as later developments such as the [[Gene-centered view of evolution|selfish gene hypothesis]]. Svensson also criticised Noble's claim that [[genetic mutations]] were directed and purposeful, contrary to the mainstream consensus that mutations are entirely [[Stochastic|random]]. Noble had, in Svensson's view, failed to present a viable alternative to natural selection, with Svensson stating it was "unclear if [Noble's proposed mechanism for evolution] is even a scientific one".<ref name="Svensson 2023" /><ref>{{Cite journal

==Awards and honours==
His major invited lectures include the Darwin Lecture for the [[British Association]] in 1966,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Noble | first1 = D | year = 1966 | title = The Initiation of the Heart Beat. (Darwin Lecture, British Association) | journal = The Advancement of Science | volume = 23 | pages = 412–418 }}</ref> the Nahum Lecture at [[Yale]] in 1977 and the Ueda lecture at [[Tokyo University]] in 1985 and 1990.  He was President of the Medical Section of the [[British Association|British Science Association]] 1991–92. Many further invited lectures during his election as Secretary-General (1993–2001) and President (2009–2017) of [[International Union of Physiological Sciences|IUPS]].

In 1979 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]]. His nomination for the Royal Society reads: {{centered pull quote|Distinguished for the discovery of [[Cardiac transient outward potassium current|slowly activated potassium currents in the heart]] and a quantitative analysis of their role in controlling [[repolarization]] and pacemaker activity; the discovery of the [[ion]]ic mechanisms by which [[adrenaline]] increases [[heart rate]]. He has shown that therapeutic levels of [[cardiac glycoside]]s may increase, rather than decrease, [[potassium]] gradients in the heart, and has published an analytical treatment of [[Cardiac action potential|membrane excitation theory]] and cable theory that provides a modern basis for the concepts of safety factor, liminal length, excitation time constants and the phenomenon of repetitive firing.<ref name="royal">{{cite web |url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo==%27EC%2F1979%2F28%27) |title=EC/1979/28: Noble, Denis |publisher=The Royal Society |archivedate=30 May 2014 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20140530133026/https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqCmd=show.tcl&dsqSearch=(RefNo=='EC/1979/28') |location=London |url-status=dead|access-date=30 May 2014 }}</ref>}}

He was elected an Honorary Member of the [[Royal College of Physicians]] in 1988 and an Honorary Fellow in 1994, an Honorary Member of the [[American Physiological Society]] in 1996 and of the Physiological Society of Japan in 1998. In 1989 he was elected a Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]. In 1998, he also became a founding Fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/professor-denis-noble/ | title=Professor Denis Noble &#124; the Academy of Medical Sciences | access-date=1 May 2015 | archive-date=3 March 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303234151/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/professor-denis-noble/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1998 he was awarded a [[Order of the British Empire|CBE]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/queens-birthday-honours-1998-1164586.html | title=Queen's Birthday honours 1998| website=[[Independent.co.uk]]| date=1998-06-12}}</ref> In 2021 he was elected a Fellow of the IUPS Academy. In 2022 he was elected a Fellow of The [[Linnean Society]] (FLS)

He has honorary doctorates from the [[University of Sheffield]] (2004),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://calendar.dept.shef.ac.uk/calendar/21_hon_grad.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=1 May 2015 |archive-date=29 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029192732/http://calendar.dept.shef.ac.uk/calendar/21_hon_grad.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[Université de Bordeaux]] (2005) and the [[University of Warwick]] (2008).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/alumni/ouralumni/hongrads/allhongrads/ |title=Our honorary graduates |access-date=1 May 2015 |archive-date=13 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113004209/https://www2.warwick.ac.uk/alumni/ouralumni/hongrads/allhongrads/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He is an Honorary Foreign Member of the [[:fr:Académie royale de médecine de Belgique|Académie Royale de Médecine de Belgique]] (1993),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.armb.be/index.php?eID=tx_nawsecuredl&u=0&g=0&hash=9b3bbce437184c4e213127eb735def496c70980b&file=fileadmin%2Fsites%2Farmb%2Fupload%2Farmb_super_editor%2Farmb_editor%2Fpdf%2FBulletin_de_l_Academie%2F2012%2Ftableau_Acad_1.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=16 February 2022 |archive-date=21 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200721185652/http://www.armb.be/index.php?eID=tx_nawsecuredl&u=0&g=0&hash=9b3bbce437184c4e213127eb735def496c70980b&file=fileadmin%2Fsites%2Farmb%2Fupload%2Farmb_super_editor%2Farmb_editor%2Fpdf%2FBulletin_de_l_Academie%2F2012%2Ftableau_Acad_1.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]], and received the Pavlov Medal of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (2004). In 2022 he was elected Foreign Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] and was also awarded the [[Lomonosov Gold Medal]].<ref>[https://www.ras.ru/news/shownews.aspx?id=8caa02a0-74b3-40c8-86a5-09200303a8b2 Lomonosov Gold Medal 2022 (in Russian)]</ref>

==Personal life==

Noble was born in London in 1936 to tailors George and Ethel Noble.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://channillo.com/series/who-am-i-who-are-you-/752-4855|title=George Noble}}</ref>

He plays classical guitar and sings [[Occitan language|Occitan]] troubadour and folk songs (Oxford Trobadors<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oxfordtrobadors.com/|title=Oxford Trobadors|website=www.oxfordtrobadors.com|access-date=15 April 2019}}</ref>). In addition to English, he has lectured in French, Italian,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oxfordtrobadors.com/StoryOc.html|title=Oxford Trobadors|website=www.oxfordtrobadors.com|access-date=15 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=4922906717795243|title=Dordogne-Périgord, le Département |website=[[Facebook]] }}</ref> Japanese and Korean.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biovision.org/speaker-info.html/26-denis-noble|title=Biovision Conference Programme|website=biovision.org|access-date=15 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725080312/http://www.biovision.org/speaker-info.html/26-denis-noble|archive-date=25 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
In 2011, [[Alison MacLeod]]'s story, "The Heart of Denis Noble", featuring a fictionalised version of Denis Noble recovering from a heart attack, was shortlisted for the [[BBC National Short Story Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BBC National Short Story Award |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/articles/2YnlfzMWv242HnQJLTcPLgR/the-2016-award |access-date=8 October 2018 |website=bbc.co.uk}}</ref>
